Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.

66: with the PRISM SIT macro in the upper-right corner, 65 placed the core's output-mux paths 1 to 2 ns short at max_tt (upstream's margin there was +0.54 ns) while 66 met every corner the resizer repairs; the target density is the placement seed here, the standard-cell utilization is 64 % either way.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
Setup slack margin - set resizer to ignore the slow corners, but add plenty of margin.

PRISM State Information Table as a hard macro: CFGMEM8x44 (DFFRAM.librelane models/cfgmem_gf, 8 words x 44 bits of latches, 595.28 x 50.96 um), flush in the upper-right corner of the core (x 841.68..1436.96, y 682.08..733.04; the tile's pins are on the left half of the top edge). The macro's Metal4 power pins were built on the tile's stripe grid (VPWR at 19.68 + k x 38.87, VGND +3.3), and Project.ExtendPowerStripes (librelane_plugin_prism_macro.py, odb_stripes.py) runs the tile's stripes over them after pdngen; pdn_macro.tcl would add a stripe for any pin column off the grid (none here). src/user_peripherals/prism/cfgmem8x44.v is the behavioural model for simulation and lint.
pdngen's connectivity check runs before Project.ExtendPowerStripes connects the macro's Metal4 pin columns (PSM-0038 on each of them); LVS is the verdict.

Hold at the slow corners: the ui_in pads reach their synchronizer flops 7.5 ns after the clock edge (base.sdc) but the clock tree takes 8.2 ns at max_ss (-0.33 ns hold, 5 pads; +3 ns at tt/ff, so RSZ_CORNERS' repair never sees them). Project.HoldRepairSlowCorner (librelane_plugin_prism_macro.py) runs a hold-only repair pass at these corners after the post-GRT resizer.
1.2 ns: the pass works on global-routing estimates and the final extraction put the clock 0.8 ns later at the worst ui_in flop than the estimate (run 3: repaired to +0.1, signed off at -0.92).

No signal routing on Metal4 over the macro: the abstract hides only the macro's own stripe columns there, so the global router would otherwise send nets through and short the tile's stripes (the LISA chip's gf11).
